### `/bin/program_nodes.sh`

59 行

````diff
--- a//bin/program_nodes.sh
+++ b//bin/program_nodes.sh
@@ -21,6 +21,25 @@
 NODE=""
 PROGRESS_FILE=/tmp/progress
 persistent_storage=/data
+
+# Product type number for X2D 100C
+X2D_100C_PRODUCT_TYPE_NUM=4
+# Product type number for CFV 100C
+CFV_100C_PRODUCT_TYPE_NUM=5
+
+# Function: product_version
+# ==================================
+# This function returns the product type number
+product_version()
+{
+    # Get the hardware version
+    #  - Format 04.04.01.04 (Product type, PCB/Hw type, ddr type, YY)
+    HW_INFO=$(getprop ro.boot.hw_version)
+    PRODUCT_TYPE=${HW_INFO:0:2}
+    PRODUCT_TYPE_NUM=$(($PRODUCT_TYPE))
+
+    echo $PRODUCT_TYPE_NUM
+}
 
 # Function: wait_for_exmcu_to_become_active
 # =========================================
@@ -67,8 +86,29 @@
 NODE="exMCU bootloader"
 /system/bin/send_fw --partition BootUpgrade --file /etc/firmware/exMCUloader.cont
 
+product=$(product_version)
+if [ $product -eq $CFV_100C_PRODUCT_TYPE_NUM ]; then
+    if [ -f /system/bin/upgrade_cpld.sh ]; then
+        cpld_fw="/etc/firmware/ec2107_cpld.bit"
+        NODE="CPLD"
+        /system/bin/upgrade_cpld.sh ${cpld_fw}
+    fi
+fi
+
+# Determine which exMCU FW image that should be sent
+if [ $product -eq $X2D_100C_PRODUCT_TYPE_NUM ]; then
+    echo "Selecting exMCU for X2D"
+    exmcu_container="/etc/firmware/exMCU_x2.cont"
+elif [ $product -eq $CFV_100C_PRODUCT_TYPE_NUM ]; then
+    echo "Selecting exMCU for CFV"
+    exmcu_container="/etc/firmware/exMCU_cfv.cont"
+else
+    echo "Unknown product version $product!"
+    exmcu_container=""
+fi
+
 NODE="exMCU"
-/system/bin/send_fw --partition ApplicationUpgrade --file /system/etc/firmware/exMCU.cont && /system/bin/send_fw -r
+/system/bin/send_fw --partition ApplicationUpgrade --file ${exmcu_container} && /system/bin/send_fw -r
 
 echo "======= End upgrade nodes ======="
 
````

+# Function to detect the product(EC1706/EC2107/EC2108)
+function product_detect

+    local hw_ver_number=""
+    local product_id=""

+        hw_ver_number=$(echo $hw_ver_str | busybox awk '{printf $2}')
+        product_id=$(echo ${hw_ver_number%%.*})
+
+        if [ "$product_id" == "04" ]; then
+            product_name="EC1706"
+        elif [ "$product_id" == "05" ]; then
+            product_name="EC2107"
+        elif [ "$product_id" == "07" ]; then
+            product_name="EC2108"
+        else
+            product_name="Unknown"
+        fi
+    fi
+
+    echo $product_name
 }

 ### wait_for_log(pattern, seconds)
 # Wait for a log print to appear in logcat
+# NOTE: Use wait_for_logcat_from if there is any risk the log print
+#       may come before the previous command finished
 wait_for_logcat() {
     local pattern="$1"

@@ -118,7 +123,68 @@

-### run_cmd_and_wait_logcat(key, pattern, seconds)
+### wait_for_logcat_from(pattern, from, seconds)
+# Wait for a log print to appear in logcat between 'from' and now+seconds
+# Use from=$(date +'%m-%d %H:%M:%S.000') before calling this function
+wait_for_logcat_from() {
+    local pattern="$1"
+    local from="$2"
+    local seconds="$3"
+    timeout $seconds logcat -T "$from" | grep -qE "$pattern"
+    if [ $? -ne $RET_OK ]; then
+        echo "Timeout after $seconds: \"$pattern\" not found in logcat"
+        return $RET_ERROR
+    fi
+    return $RET_OK
+}
+
+### match_logcat_from(from, pattern, arg1, arg2, ... argN)
+# Extract all lines containing pattern, between times from and now.
+# And in those lines, match the remaining arguments in the given order.
+# The number of arguments must be the same as the number of lines captured with pattern
+# Example, lines:
+#   monkey eats banana
+#   elephant trumpets
+#   monkey throws peel
+#   tiger roars
+# match_logcat <from> monkey eats throws
+#  will match, but
+# match_logcat <from> monkey eats
+#  will not match
+match_logcat_from() {
+    local from=$1
+    local pattern=$2
+    shift; shift
+    lines=$(logcat -t "$from" | grep -E "$pattern")
+    local count=$(echo -n "$lines" | grep -c "^")
+
+    if [ "$count" -ne "$#" ]; then
+        echo "Incorrect number of pattern matches. matched=$count, expected=$#"
+        echo "$lines"
+        return "$RET_ERROR"
+    fi
+
+    # Build a match string from all the remaining arguments
+    local match="$1"
+    shift
+    while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
+        match+=".*$1"
+        shift
+    done
+
+    result=$(echo "$lines" | grep -qz "$match")
+    ret=$?
+    if [ "$ret" -ne 0 ]; then
+        echo "Failed to match $match in"
+        echo "$lines"
+    else
+        echo "Successful match of arguments in"
+        echo "$lines"
+    fi
+    return $?
+}
+
+### run_cmd_and_wait_logcat(cmd, pattern, seconds)
 # Start command in background and wait for logcat
 # immediately to avoid the risk of missing a log that comes
 # before the command exits.
@@ -182,3 +248,59 @@
     result=$(find /mnt/media_rw/"${storage}"/ -name "*.${format}" | wc -l)
     echo "${result}"
 }
+
+### get_property(service, property)
+# Retrieve given property value, but strip the property name from response
+get_property() {
+    local service=$1
+    local property=$2
+    local value
+
+    if ! value=$(odindb-send --print-cmdline -s $service -p $property); then
+        return ${RET_ERROR}
+    fi
+
+    # ${value} is now in format "<property> = <value>", lets strip it to <value>
+    echo ${value} | cut -d"=" -f2 | xargs
+    return ${RET_OK}
+}
+
+## wait_property_value(service, property, desired_value, timeout)
+# Poll given property value continuously until its value becomes
+# <desired_value> or timeout elapses.
+#
+# Returns $RET_OK if value == <desired_value>
+# Returns $RET_ERROR if timeout occurs before value becomes <desired_value>
+# Returns $RET_ERROR if unable to read property
+wait_property_value() {
+    local service="$1"
+    local property="$2"
+    local desired_value="$3"
+    local tmo="$4"
+
+    echo -n "Waiting ${tmo}s for ${service}::${property} == ${desired_value}..."
+    start_time=$(date +%s)
+    end_time=$((start_time + tmo))
+    while true; do
+        local value
+        if ! value=$(get_property "${service}" "${property}"); then
+            echo "error: failed to read property ${service}::${property}" >&2
+            return ${RET_ERROR}
+        fi
+
+        if [ "${value}" = "${desired_value}" ]; then
+            echo "OK!"
+            return ${RET_OK}
+        fi
+
+        if [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "${end_time}" ]; then
+            echo "error: timeout waiting for property ${property} to " \
+                 "become '${desired_value}' (${value})" >&2
+            return ${RET_ERROR}
+        fi
+
+        echo -n "."
+        timeout -s HUP 0.5 odindb-send -s ${service} \
+            --signal-oneshot "${property}Changed" > /dev/null
+    done
+}

+# Reconfigures E2 pin connected to FSYNC to GPIO and waits for pulse (IRQ)

+function listen_e2_fsync_irq
+{
+    local timeout
+    local result
+
+    local fsync_pin=GB_GPIO0_4
+
+    timeout=$1
+

+    if [[ "${result}" == "Failed to wait" ]]; then
+        echo "fail" > "${FSYNC_IRQ}"
+    else
+        echo "ok" > "${FSYNC_IRQ}"

+        fi

+    rm -f "${FSYNC_IRQ}"
+    [[ "${result}" == "ok" ]]

+[ienc:hevc]
+    dump_stream_buffer = false
+
 [ienc:frwk]

     name = hw_imgtec
